record.paper_title: Operations Research challenges in forestry: 33 open problems
record.original_question: Cell-based area restriction models for harvest scheduling must limit contiguous disturbed area while handling many cells, many periods, and potentially road-building and maintenance decisions. The open question is how to develop exact formulations and exact solution methods for these large ARM instances at realistic forestry scales.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 12 How can we develop exact models and methods for the ARM for large-scale problems involving thousands of cells and many time periods, along with road building and maintenance decisions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a forest landscape partitioned into a finite set $V$ of management cells, with a planar adjacency graph $G=(V,E)$ in which two cells are adjacent if and only if they share a boundary of positive length. A planning horizon is divided into time periods $T=\{1,\dots,P\}$. Each cell $i\in V$ has area $a_i>0$ and, for each period $t\in T$, an economic value $v_{i,t}$ that is collected if cell $i$ is harvested in period $t$. A cell may be harvested at most once over the horizon. After harvest, a cell remains "disturbed" (open/recently cut) for a fixed green-up duration of $g$ periods before being considered recovered.

Area Restriction Model (ARM). The ARM imposes that in every period $t\in T$, any connected component (in the subgraph of $G$ induced by currently disturbed cells) of contiguous disturbed cells has total area at most a prescribed maximum opening size $A_{\max}$. Note that this is genuinely combinatorial: contiguous clusters of harvested cells are allowed up to $A_{\max}$, but their composition is not fixed a priori (in contrast with the Unit Restriction Model).

Roads. Superimposed on $V$ is a road network represented by a graph $H=(N,R)$ whose nodes $N\supseteq V$ include cell access points and existing/potential road junctions, with arcs $R$ representing potential road segments. Each segment $r\in R$ has a construction cost $c_r$ and a per-period maintenance cost $m_{r,t}$. In order to harvest cell $i$ in period $t$, there must exist in period $t$ a path of built and maintained road segments in $H$ from a designated mill/exit node to the access point of $i$. Once built, a segment may be maintained or temporarily closed in subsequent periods; the cost structure $(c_r,m_{r,t})$ is given.

Objective. Maximize the discounted net revenue
$$\sum_{i\in V}\sum_{t\in T} v_{i,t}\, x_{i,t} \;-\;\sum_{r\in R}\Bigl( c_r\, y_r + \sum_{t\in T} m_{r,t}\, z_{r,t}\Bigr),$$
where $x_{i,t}\in\{0,1\}$ indicates harvesting cell $i$ in period $t$, $y_r\in\{0,1\}$ indicates building segment $r$ at some time, and $z_{r,t}\in\{0,1\}$ indicates that segment $r$ is active in period $t$, subject to the ARM contiguity/area constraints, the green-up constraints, the road-access constraints, and standard logical linking constraints between $x$, $y$, $z$.

Problem. Develop an exact mixed-integer programming formulation, together with an exact solution method (e.g., branch-and-bound, branch-and-cut, branch-and-price, or decomposition), that is provably correct for the above ARM-with-roads problem and is able to solve to proven optimality (or with a certified optimality gap) instances with thousands of cells ($|V|\ge 10^3$) and many time periods (e.g., $P\ge 10$), with simultaneous road-building and road-maintenance decisions, at realistic forestry scales.
artifact.status_search_result: Exact branch-and-price methods exist for ARM harvest scheduling (e.g., cluster/path/bucket formulations) and have been tested on instances up to roughly 2,900 stands and 12 periods without roads, while separate models address integrated harvest-and-road planning, often via heuristics/metaheuristics or only on small/medium instances. No published exact method appears to scale to thousands of cells with many periods while jointly handling road-building and maintenance, so the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: A branch-and-price approach for harvest scheduling subject to maximum area restrictions
status_evidence.snippet: Branch-and-price was tested on real and hypothetical forests ranging from 45 to 2945 stands and temporal horizons ranging from three to twelve periods.
status_evidence.claim: Exact branch-and-price exists for pure ARM up to ~2945 stands, but does not address simultaneous road-building/maintenance decisions.

status_evidence.title: Harvest Scheduling Subject to Maximum Area Restrictions: Exploring Exact Approaches
status_evidence.snippet: Three main basic integer programming models (cluster, path, bucket) are discussed; solving via branch-and-bound is suited only to small/medium problems.
status_evidence.claim: Exact branch-and-bound on standard ARM formulations does not scale to large instances.

status_evidence.title: Solving the integrated forest harvest scheduling model using metaheuristic algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: Integrated harvest-and-road planning models are commonly attacked with metaheuristics due to size.
status_evidence.claim: Integrated ARM-with-roads problems at realistic scale are typically solved heuristically, indicating the exact version remains open.
